messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] eu-west-2 monitoring probe failure spike — 18/03 09:12 UTC. 12 healthchecks failed in last 2m, alerting on-call.
Alice K: got it, I'm on it. digging into the probe dashboard now.
Alice K: quick look — synthetic DNS probes from eu-west-2 show timeouts and some 502s, but a lot of the probe metrics are missing entirely from the collector.
Ben M: are we seeing real customer errors or just probe noise?
Alice K: early data: API requests served from eu-west-2 show a small uptick in 5xxs (~4.8% of p50 traffic) and increased latency for some routes. looks correlated with probe failures but not identical.
Carla S: could be probe agents losing connectivity to collector. Any recent deployment to the probe fleet?
Alice K: no deploys in eu-west-2 last hour. config unchanged.
Dmitry P: can someone run a dig + curl to the regional healthcheck endpoints from an external VM? my hunch is DNS resolution intermittency.
Alice K: running dig now from jumpbox: ```dig +short api.eu-west-2.redwood.internal @8.8.8.8```
Alice K: result: intermittent NXDOMAIN on first query, second succeeds. traceroute shows packet loss at the regional edge (two hops in).
Ben M: route53 health checks show flapping for the region, but the healthcheck logs are missing many entries between 09:08-09:11 UTC — looks like telemetry gap.
incident-bot: Created incident INC-2026-0243 (severity: P2) — "eu-west-2 probe/telemetry gap causing healthcheck flapping". Incident channel: #inc-2026-0243.
Alice K: I'm going to silence noisy probe alerts while we investigate so oncall isn't flooded. /incident silence eu-west-2-probes 30m — please confirm if you see the silence command.
Support Bot: Alerts for eu-west-2-probes silenced by Alice K for 30 minutes.
Carla S: grabbing VPC flow logs + ENI metrics for the probe subnet. also checking if any SG/NACL changes were pushed.
Dmitry P: pinging cloud provider support — opening ticket. sending them packet captures and traceroutes.
Ben M: routing table looks fine on our side. but I see an increase in dropped packets in the edge NAT gateways in the provider telemetry. forwarding to provider.
Alice K: customer impact: calculated from request logs — about 4.8% error rate region-wide for 09:06-09:16 UTC, spike concentrated on small subset of endpoints. impacting some streaming/long-polling flows. marking D1 customers potentially affected.
Carla S: flow logs show sporadic ICMP unreachable then normal. suggests an intermittent edge filtering rule or overloaded edge.
Dmitry P: provider replied: "We observe transient control-plane instability in eu-west-2 edge, affecting health checks and external DNS resolution; mitigation rolling." asking for timeframe.
Ben M: while provider mitigates, we should enable regional fallback routing for critical customers. proposing to route traffic to eu-west-1 for those pinned customers via failover policy.
Alice K: agree. initiating canary failover for customer buckets with >50% requests from eu-west-2. will update runbook and open rollback steps.
Alice K: handing off to Ben for active mitigation and provider comms — I'm going to scope post-incident notes and start a retrospective doc. Ben, please update #inc-2026-0243 with status and ETA from provider.
Ben M: taking over. summary for next oncall: telemetry gap caused probe floods and false positives. provider working on edge instability. action items assigned in incident channel. ETA from provider ~20-40m.
Alice K: thanks — going to bed but reachable on pager. please escalate to SRE lead if severity increases. :phone: :sleeping:emoji:
Ben M: noted. I'll coordinate with Carla and Dmitry.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0243 updated: assigned -> Ben M; severity unchanged P2.
Carla S: added puppet ACL check to tasks list to rule out accidental rule pushes.
Dmitry P: provider reports partial mitigation at 09:30 UTC — health checks recovering, DNS resolution stabilizing. continuing to monitor.
Ben M: marking this thread as active handoff. will close when metrics stable and provider confirms full resolution.
Alice K: thanks team.
Support Bot: Thread archived to /incidents/2026/INC-2026-0243 once closed.
